claims.explanation: Digoxin's primary target is the Na+/K+-ATPase (ATP1A1), and its cytotoxic selectivity likely reflects dependence on ATP1A1-mediated ion homeostasis and downstream signaling rather than a single lineage. Lines with high ATP1A1 expression or specific oncogenic contexts (e.g., KRAS-mutant pancreatic, NRF2/NFE2L2-mutant squamous, or ARID1A-mutant lines) appear enriched among sensitive lines, while some bladder, mesothelioma, and certain EGFR-mutant lung lines are relatively resistant. The pattern suggests that ATP1A1 expression level and NFE2L2/KEAP1 pathway status are key determinants of digoxin sensitivity.

features.basis: Digoxin directly inhibits ATP1A1; higher target expression increases drug effect
NFE2L2-mutant squamous lines (KYSE70, KYSE520, HEC265) are enriched among sensitive lines
KEAP1 mutation co-occurs with NFE2L2 activation in sensitive endometrial line HEC265
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and lung lines are enriched among sensitive lines
ARID1A mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines (SUIT2, KYSE70, SW1088, HS766T, OVK18)
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so not selective; listed as weak negative evidence
EGFR-mutant lung line NCIH1650 is among least affected lines
SMARCA4-mutant lines COV434 and FTC238 are among least affected
PTEN mutations appear in several resistant lines (A2058, FTC238, SNU466)
CDKN2A mutations appear in several resistant lines (SCABER, KELLY, ASPC1, RD)
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines SH4 and IGR37 are sensitive, while BRAF/PTEN-mutant A2058 is resistant, suggesting context dependence
NRAS-mutant lines NCIH1299 and SW1088 are sensitive, but NRAS-mutant RD is resistant, so weak evidence
